notes: First Q-simple, geometrically split example of [2,2,2,6] for the census (the gsplit cell is empty). Construction: quadratic-conjugate (2,2)-gluing. E = E_{2,6}(t) (Tate normal form of HLP Table 3) with t = (11 + 84*sqrt(-11))/37 over K = Q(sqrt(-11)), E(K)_tors = Z/2 x Z/6, glued with its Galois conjugate E^sigma along the G_K-isomorphism E[2] -> E^sigma[2], T_i -> sigma(T_i) (it satisfies psi^sigma psi = id, so the glued surface and the curve descend to Q). The parameter was chosen so that the Kummer classes of both generators of E(K)_tors/2 are sigma-invariant: N(t-3), N((t-5)(t+3)) and N((t-9)(t-1)) are squares in Q (norms from K); this doubles the torsion twice, J(Q)_tors = [2,2,2,6] against [2,6] for a generic member. E is not a Q-curve (a_P(E) <> a_P(E^sigma) at 13 of 32 split primes below 400), so J is simple over Q (also certified by chi_29 irreducible); J is (2,2)-isogenous over Q to Res_{K/Q} E, which Magma's Richelot search finds. Magma's Conductor on the reduced minimal model: 2^2 * 3^2 * 5^2 * 7^2 * 11^2 * 23 * 37^2. Rigorous conductor: J is (2,2)-isogenous over Q to Res_(K/Q) E with K the quadratic field of discriminant -11, so N(J) = |d_K|^2 * Norm(f_E) = 121 * 1388576700 = 168017780700 (computed with Magma; conductor is an isogeny invariant).
